title: Lineup player references persist as a nullable playerId that only repositories map
decision: Lineup slots persist the player reference as a nullable ObjectId `playerId` instead of an explicit `_id` path, and an empty slot is stored as `{ playerId: null, position }`. Repositories are the sole translation boundary: reads map `playerId` to domain `id: string | null` and writes map it back, for team lineups and for every embedded game reference (set lineups, player and staff snapshots, rally details and substitution `players.in/out`). Domain entities, Zod schemas, Redux and React keep using `id` only.
context: Lineup player subschemas disabled their own `_id` and then declared the player reference on an explicit `_id` ObjectId path. Because the `id` virtual is read-only, writes silently dropped the reference, and the game read path mapped only the top-level `_id`, leaving nested references unmapped.

alternatives.reason: Avoids a schema rename, but creates a second, fragile nested mapping path and does not fix the dropped writes.
Avoids ObjectId conversion, but diverges from the reference conventions and loses ObjectId validation and join semantics.
No migration, but it cannot represent an empty reference and keeps the write-drop bug.

consequences: Existing references move through the audit-first migration of ADR-0139.
The shared lineup schema changes team and game documents together, so both repository mappings move in one change.
